qs.q:
What would you invent to make the world a better place? — Which person…

A=Anna (cellular immunity theory, needs research, dad sparked the idea, father runs pharmaceutical company)
B=Benjamin (invent law mandating exercise+nutrition, go into parliament, support from family for business partners)
C=Chris (brain device 'Progressor' combining biology+technology, would speed up scientific discoveries)
D=Daphne (food cloning machine to end hunger, team up with scientists and celebrities, ethical doubts, profitable)
E=Ebony (toy for every kid, volunteer group with recycled materials, free worldwide distribution, message of caring)
F=Ferdinand (nanotechnology nanorobot for time management, inspired by novel, needs global computer corporation)

0. needs more proof for her/his theory? [A=Anna]
1. would need an international company as a partner?
2. would start a non-profit social project?
3. would like to influence the education system?
4. would have little difficulty with funding?
5. was partly inspired by fiction?
6. would invent a cybernetic device?
7. thinks people are actually caring?
8. has done research on biotechnology?
9. would like to enhance human mental powers?
10. was motivated by a family member?
11. would go into politics?
12. has some moral issues about his/her invention?
items: 1 — would need an international company as a partner?
2 — would start a non-profit social project?
3 — would like to influence the education system?
4 — would have little difficulty with funding?
9 — would like to enhance human mental powers?
10 — was motivated by a family member?
12 — has some moral issues about his/her invention?

qs.q:
Husky sledding in the Arctic

"I hadn't realised it was the VISITORS that were mad."

What did the author of the text dislike when he arrived in Lapland?
A The tourists were too keen on celebrating Christmas.
B It was too dark for most of the day in the Arctic Circle.
C He would have to wait for a week before he saw the sun again.
D The airport was too crowded with English tourists.
opts: The tourists were too keen on celebrating Christmas.
It was too dark for most of the day in the Arctic Circle.
He would have to wait for a week before he saw the sun again.
The airport was too crowded with English tourists.

qs.q:
What I wish I had known when I was younger

"We worry too much about what people around us think of us. (19) ____. Everyone around you has an opinion, but in reality, others' opinions are based more on their history than anything you're actually doing."

A Therefore, when you hear about an overnight triumph story, be aware of all the work that came before.
B If it does not bring you happiness, it will, at worst, help you be miserable in comfort.
C That is more than a fine stretch to fit a whole host of wonderful endeavours into your life.
D If you waste too much time seeking validation, respect or approval from them, you won't have time to accomplish all that you desire.
E Consequently, such thoughts serve the purpose of knocking down the obstacles in your way.
F Evidently, dishonesty, disrespect, unhappiness and evil exist and you will have to deal with them.
G This goes to say that you can't influence unmet expectations, bygone situations and failures.
H Nor does it insulate you from pain, suffering and conflict.
opts: A — Be aware of all the work that came before overnight success.
B — It will help you be miserable in comfort.
C — A fine stretch to fit a whole host of wonderful endeavours.
D — Wasting time seeking validation means you won't accomplish what you desire.
E — Such thoughts serve to knock down obstacles.
F — Dishonesty and evil exist and you will have to deal with them.
G — You can't influence unmet expectations and past failures.
H — Nor does it insulate you from pain and conflict.
